newsitem.title: CHINA: China city Jan-July foreign funds up 29 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: China city Jan-July foreign funds up 29 pct yr/yr.

text.p: The registered capital of foreign-funded companies in China's eastern boom town of Shanghai rose 29.07 percent in January-July compared with the same period a year ago, the Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.
Registered capital of Chinese private firms in the city grew by a year-on-year 23.36 percent in the period, Xinhua said without elaborating.
The city's state-owned sector registered a drop in capital, the first such decline, the agency said.
The increased profitability of the Shanghai market had fuelled the rise in foreign capital, it said.
Stricter capital auditing measures and a rise in bankruptcies had contributed to the capital decline in the state sector, it said.
Xinhua quoted analysts as saying the decline would continue for some time but would not adversely affect Shanghai's economy.
Shanghai's industrial output in the first seven months rose by 15.5 percent compared with the year-ago period, while output of the state-owned sector was up 11.8 percent, Xinhua said.
